why: Quote verified verbatim: champion-kit.md line 129, third row of the 'Patterns that tend to work' table; the whole line is a three-cell row ('Generate a setup guide from your own usage' | the quoted text | 'About two minutes') and neither neighbouring cell reverses it. So the finding is not refuted on the quote. It is refuted on the page it cites and on its claim about our state. (1) WRONG CONTRACT PAGE. champion-kit is an internal-advocacy playbook for engineers evangelising Claude Code; our own coverage map already carries its verdict at 2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:232 (row 116): '⬜ вне продукта; вердикт записан' — out of product, verdict recorded. The behaviour contract for the command is commands.md (corpus row 83 in scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv; coverage-map row 38 at :109, marked 🟩 fully read). (2) THE CONTRACT PAGE SHOWS A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. commands.md:139 verbatim: 'Generate a team onboarding guide from your Claude Code usage history. Claude analyzes your sessions, commands, and MCP server usage from the past 30 days and produces a markdown guide a teammate can paste as a first message to get set up quickly. For claude.ai subscribers on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, also returns a share link teammates can open directly in Claude Code'. The delivery half is claude.ai Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise-gated and runs on Anthropic-hosted org infrastructure (the backing harness tool is ShareOnboardingGuide, which uploads ONBOARDING.md to an org guide and returns a share link). This fork drops claude.ai subscription flows by design. (3) 'NO RECORDED DEFERRAL' IS FALSE, IN FOUR PLACES. (a) 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1710-1711: 'Explicitly judged inapplicable, recorded so nobody re-derives it: everything that needs Anthropic-hosted infrastructure or a claude.ai tier — remote control, mobile, web, artifacts, routines, ultraplan/ultrareview, and the Artifact/RemoteTrigger/ShareOnboardingGuide tools.' (b) 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:268: 'NOT OURS TO BUILD: RemoteTrigger/Routines (claude.ai, Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, Anthropic-hosted) and ShareOnboardingGuide stay inapplicable, consistent with §5e-2.' (c) This same 2026-08-02 sweep's own whats-new/2026-w15 row (2026-08-02-claude-doc-sweep-divergences.md:441, and its source 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3338) names /team-onboarding explicitly: 'Ultraplan, /autofix-pr, /team-onboarding, focus view, the Bedrock/Vertex wizards and the status-line keys ... bind cloud or TUI surfaces we do not ship.' (d) This same sweep's `commands` page row (:382) read the full built-in command table and recorded the scoped position — 'Nessy is a GUI, so most terminal-only entries are out of scope' — enumerating the shipped subset (/compact, /context, /clear, /export, /init, /memory, /model, /usage, /help, /agents, /subtask plus /mcp__<server>__<prompt>); the one divergence it filed from that page is a leading-command parsing rule, not /team-onboarding. So f128 re-files, from an out-of-product advocacy page, something the sweep had already judged on the contract page. (4) CONSEQUENCE CHECKED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER. The identifier really is absent — confirmed with grep -a, hits only in sweep artefacts and the coverage-map description at :281, which says exactly what was claimed. But the consequence 'a missing command' is wrong at the tier level: this fork has no built-in slash-command tier at all. packages/shared/src/slash-commands/ contains only session-command.ts (/compact, /subtask), custom-commands.ts, mcp-prompt-commands and subtask.ts; Claude's built-in commands land here either as bundled skills (packages/shared/src/config/bundled-skills-settings.ts) or, for /doctor, as a session-free CLI subcommand `nessy-general-agent doctor` (audit R30b), never as a built-in command. /team-onboarding has no host tier to be missing from. It is a catalogue-level product-scope position, not a per-command omission. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — those are nine identifier-level inert-contract decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) and this is not among them; the recorded decisions that do cover it are the two named in (3a) and (3b).
correctedState: The quote is verbatim (champion-kit.md:129), and /team-onboarding is indeed absent from this fork. But champion-kit is an out-of-product advocacy playbook whose coverage-map verdict is already recorded (coverage-map row 116); the command's actual contract page is commands.md:139, which was read in this same sweep and whose scoped verdict ('Nessy is a GUI, so most terminal-only entries are out of scope') covers it. The share-link half is claude.ai Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise-gated and backed by ShareOnboardingGuide, a tool twice recorded as inapplicable/not-ours-to-build (parity-audit:1710-1711; r-queue-doc-verification:268), consistent with this fork dropping claude.ai subscription flows. This fork ships no built-in slash-command tier at all (only /compact and /subtask as session commands, plus custom, plugin/skill and MCP-prompt commands), so there is no tier for /team-onboarding to be missing from. Not a defect and not undeclared: a recorded product-scope decision. The only honest residual, which f128 does not claim, is that the LOCAL generation half (scan 30 days of local sessions, commands and MCP usage into a markdown guide) needs no Anthropic infrastructure and could in principle be built as a bundled skill; if anyone wants it, file it against commands.md:139, not champion-kit.
